newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close down 0.2 pct in listless trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close down 0.2 pct in listless trading.

text.p: Brazil shares closed down 0.22 percent in a quiet session in which foreigners showed little interest and major domestic investors reorganizing their portfolios, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares dropped 142 points to close at 66,127 points. Turnover was a light 305.3 million ($298.9 million).
Traders expect the bourse to open mixed on Tuesday with a continuing lack of foreign interest.
"Foreign investors are remaining on the sidelines awaiting the end of the second-round of the municipal elections (on Nov 15)," the trader said.

Power firms were again the big winners. Electricity firm Cemig, controlled by the Minas Gerais state government, preferred shares ended up 1.26 percent at 32.20 reais. State power firm Eletrobras common shares rose 1.05 percent to close at 290 reais. The preferred share ELE_p.SA ended at 303 reais, up 0.33 percent.

Analysts attributed the rise to an auction earlier today in the foward market in which BNDESPar, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank, sold off 0.28 percent of Eletrobras voting capital for an average price of 309.32 reais per lots of 1,000 shares.
"The auction created a good prospect for the share," a trader said.
Benchmark Telebras preferred share dropped 0.24 percent to close at 81.80 reais.
